# Pre-Registration — judgment-vs-trust bar differential

**This file is sealed by its commit. It is written and committed BEFORE any reviewer is run.** The results artifact will cite this file's commit SHA as proof the predictions preceded the data. Do not edit this file after the runs begin; record all outcomes in the separate results artifact.

## What is being tested

Single variable = the judgment-vs-trust **lens apparatus** (the `## Two Kinds of Skill` section in `agent-facing-design` + the bar-keyed step-3/severity rules in `scrutinize-skill`). Confirmed single-variable: the only reviewer-behavior diff between `3eb0e74^` and `main` on the two reviewer SKILL.md files *is* the lens (staging sanity: bar-on contract has 1 "Two Kinds of Skill" / 25 "judgment"; bar-off has 0 / 4 residual generic uses).

- **Bar-ON reviewer** = live scrutinize-skill SKILL.md + live agent-facing-design SKILL.md (step 3 = "Bar And Execution Quality"; classify part judgment/trust; on judgment parts "treat a mandated output shape, exhaustive rule list, or fixed-section conformance as a defect, not a requirement"; bar-keyed severity: conformance divergence on judgment parts drops/downgrades, thinking/provoke defects keep/escalate).
- **Bar-OFF reviewer** = scrutinize-skill@`3eb0e74^` + agent-facing-design@`3eb0e74^` (step 3 = "Execution Quality"; reviews "first move, context reading, defaults, stop conditions, handoffs, **output shape**, failure handling" UNIFORMLY for every skill; no judgment/trust split, no bar-keyed severity, no Two Kinds section).

Both configs review the **same** current-`main` target SKILL.md (frozen snapshots in `/tmp/bar-differential/targets/`). Only the reviewer contract differs.

## The prediction engine (the mechanism under test)

The bar claims to change reviews of **judgment skills that carry conformance-flaggable structure** (mandated output shapes, fixed sections, numeric caps, verdict tokens) OR conformance *gaps* (no report-style output shape). The predicted mechanism:

- Bar-OFF's uniform "Execution Quality" (which explicitly reviews "output shape") will **raise** conformance findings on judgment skills — "missing/weak output shape," "no closure," "arbitrary numeric cap could drop findings," "rigid mandated structure," "inconsistent verdict tokens."
- Bar-ON will **drop or downgrade** those same conformance findings on judgment parts (treats fixed shape as not-a-defect), while **keeping/escalating** genuine provoke-side defects (a forcing function dulled) and all **trust**-part defects.
- On **trust** skills both configs apply the same (trust) bar → **no divergence**.

## Aggregate predictions (sealed)

- **A1 — Pattern.** Divergence concentrates in rows 1-4 (PD judgment skills), in the "OFF raises / ON drops conformance" direction. Controls (6, 8) and trust-dominant mixed (9, 10) show no patterned divergence.
- **A2 — Level.** Divergence appears mostly at the **finding/severity level**, NOT the 4-level **verdict** level. I predict verdicts (Reject/Major/Minor/Defensible) are **mostly stable** across configs (most targets land Minor/Defensible under both). An analysis that looks only at verdicts could wrongly read finding-level divergence as INERT. Both levels will be scored.
- **A3 — Strongest single signal.** Row 1 (system-design-review finding-cap) is the highest-confidence divergence and the cleanest single test of the mechanism.
- **A4 — Over-cut watch.** Rows 5 and 10 are the over-cut tripwires: if bar-ON aggressively flags organizing/trust-appropriate structure (the rec packet, the acceptance-map shape) as substitutive, that is LOAD-BEARING+**WRONG**, not success.
- **A5 — Count.** Of the 5 PD/PD-ish rows (1-5) I expect **2-4** to show consistent (≥2 of 3 reps) patterned divergence. Rows 1-2 are the most likely; 3-5 are coin-flips.

## Interpretive caveats (sealed BEFORE seeing data — must survive into the results)

- **C1 — INERT is genuinely ambiguous, and I am pre-committing to report both readings.** An INERT result (bar-on ≈ bar-off) falsifies "the bar changes reviewer output" — and per the work order that is reported **loudly, not softened**. BUT it does not by itself distinguish (a) "the bar is decoration" from (b) "the underlying model **already** applies the judgment/trust distinction without the bar text, so the bar is redundant." Both are failures of the bar to *add* value, but they imply different next moves. I will report which is more likely from the bar-OFF reasoning traces (does bar-OFF spontaneously decline to flag conformance on judgment skills, citing judgment-skill reasoning it was never given?).
- **C2 — Same-model circularity is NOT escaped here.** Both reviewers are the same model; a passing differential shows the bar is *non-inert*, never that its calls are *correct*. Correctness needs tests 1 (foreign material) and 2 (human cold-judge). This limit goes in the results verbatim.
- **C3 — Stochasticity.** A single bar-on vs bar-off difference can be noise. Only **consistent, patterned** divergence (≥2 of 3 reps, same target, same direction) counts. One-off differences are logged as noise, not divergence.
- **C4 — Blind scoring is mandatory.** Paired outputs are labeled A/B at random; the comparison judge decides where they diverge WITHOUT knowing which is bar-on; only then unblind and compare to these predictions.

## Verdict rubric (from the work order)

- **INERT** — bar-on ≈ bar-off everywhere → falsification (report loudly; apply C1).
- **LOAD-BEARING + CORRECT** — divergence concentrated on predicted judgment-conformance items, predicted direction, controls + genuine defects unchanged.
- **LOAD-BEARING + WRONG** — divergence that doesn't match predictions (lenient on real defects, over-cuts organizing/trust structure, or moves trust-skill verdicts).
